CheckTitle: Ensure MFA is enabled for all IAM users that have a console password
Description: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) must be enabled for all IAM users who have a console password. Without MFA, a compromised password alone is sufficient to authenticate to the AWS Management Console.
Risk: IAM users without MFA are vulnerable to credential-based attacks (phishing, password spray, credential stuffing). A single compromised password grants full console access up to the user's permission scope with no additional authentication barrier.
Remediation: Enable MFA for each IAM user with a console password using virtual MFA (TOTP) or hardware MFA. Enforce MFA via IAM policy condition aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent for sensitive operations.
SeverityBasis: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0.0 Control 1.10 (Level 1); AWS Security Hub FSBP IAM.5 (ASFF score 64 / MEDIUM); CIS Level 1 designation and direct authentication bypass risk warrant High severity
AuthoritativeSource: CIS Amazon Web Services Foundations Benchmark v3.0.0; AWS Security Hub FSBP
